sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

Bun

Documentation   •   Discord   •   Issues   •   Roadmap
### [Read the docs →](https://bun.com/docs) ## What is Bun? Bun is an all-in-one toolkit for JavaScript and TypeScript apps. It ships as a single executable called `bun`. At its core is the _Bun runtime_, a fast JavaScript runtime designed as **a drop-in replacement for Node.js**. It's written in Rust and powered by JavaScriptCore under the hood, dramatically reducing startup times and memory usage. ```bash bun run index.tsx # TS and JSX supported out-of-the-box ``` The `bun` command-line tool also implements a test runner, script runner, and Node.js-compatible package manager. Instead of 1,000 node_modules for development, you only need `bun`. Bun's built-in tools are significantly faster than existing options and usable in existing Node.js projects with little to no changes. ```bash bun test # run tests bun run start # run the `start` script in `package.json` bun install # install a package bunx cowsay 'Hello, world!' # execute a package ``` ## Install Bun supports Linux (x64 & arm64), macOS (x64 & Apple Silicon), and Windows (x64 & arm64). > **Linux users** — Kernel version 5.6 or higher is strongly recommended, but the minimum is 5.1. > **x64 users** — if you see "illegal instruction" or similar errors, check our [CPU requirements](https://bun.com/docs/installation#cpu-requirements) ```sh # with install script (recommended) curl -fsSL https://bun.com/install | bash # on windows powershell -c "irm bun.sh/install.ps1 | iex" # with npm npm install -g bun # with Homebrew brew tap oven-sh/bun brew install bun # with Docker docker pull oven/bun docker run --rm --init --ulimit memlock=-1:-1 oven/bun ``` ### Upgrade To upgrade to the latest version of Bun, run: ```sh bun upgrade ``` Bun automatically releases a canary build on every commit to `main`. To upgrade to the latest canary build, run: ```sh bun upgrade --canary ``` [View canary build](https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/tag/canary) ## Quick links - Intro - [What is Bun?](https://bun.com/docs/index) - content.text:
The codebase of `oven-sh/bun` is a high-performance JavaScript/TypeScript runtime and toolkit written primarily in Rust. It is designed as a drop-in replacement for Node.js, utilizing JavaScriptCore (JSC) as its underlying engine.

Key components of the project include:

### 1. **Core Runtime (`src/runtime/`)**
This directory contains the heart of the Bun runtime:
- **Execution Engine**: Manages the JavaScriptCore virtual machine, handles the event loop, and manages thread-local storage.
- **CLI Dispatch**: Implements the `bun` command-line interface, including the package manager (`bun install`), test runner (`bun test`), and script runner (`bun run`).
- **Shell Interpreter**: A high-performance shell (similar to `zsh`/`sh`) that handles script execution, environment variable expansion, and signal handling.
- **System APIs**: Provides Rust-native implementations for File I/O, Networking (HTTP/TCP/UDP/WebSockets), and process management.

### 2. **Module Resolution (`src/resolver/`)**
The resolver is a sophisticated state machine that determines how imports are mapped to files. It supports:
- **Node.js Compatibility**: Correctly resolves `node_modules`, `exports` fields in `package.json`, and `.npmrc` configurations.
- **TypeScript Support**: Parses and respects `tsconfig.json` `paths` and `baseUrl`.
- **Standalone Module Graph**: A specialized resolution mode for pre-bundled executables that allows for fast, link-time resolution of dependencies.

### 3. **Bundler (`src/bundler/`)**
Bun's bundler is designed for speed and modern web features:
- **`BundleV2` Architecture**: A modern, multi-threaded bundling system that uses a graph-based approach to handle dependencies, CSS, and assets.
- **Transpilation**: Integrated support for JSX, TypeScript, and various module formats, allowing Bun to skip heavy preprocessing steps.
- **Hot Module Replacement (HMR)**: Support for fast development cycles by only re-bundling changed parts of the dependency graph.

### 4. **JavaScript API (`src/js/`)**
This area contains the "Bun-specific" JavaScript APIs (like `Bun.file`, `Bun.serve`, `Bun.sql`) and the types used to expose them to the runtime.

### 5. **Ecosystem and Plugins (`packages/`)**
The repository contains several sub-packages that extend Bun's capabilities:
- **Plugins**: Native support for Svelte, YAML, and other framework-specific bundling optimizations.
- **Inspector**: Tools for debugging Bun's runtime and providing a VS Code debugger adapter.
- **Native Bundler Plugin API**: A stable interface for third-party developers to write custom bundler plugins.

### Key Technical Patterns:
- **Memory Management**: Uses `mimalloc` with thread-local arenas to achieve high-concurrency without heavy locking.
- **Zero-Copy**: Heavily utilizes `RawSlice` and `ZStr` to share data between the Rust core and the JS engine without unnecessary allocations.
- **Stacked Borrows**: Uses the `StackedBorrows` crate to manage complex aliasing rules, allowing for safe and performant shared access to singleton resources (like the FileSystem and Loggers) across multiple worker threads.
